title: Read the right argument
starter:
let greeting (argv : string array) : string =
  "hello, " ^ argv.(0)
hints: Slot 0 of the array is the program's own name. The first word the user typed after it is in slot 1.
Check `Array.length argv` before you read slot 1. A right call has exactly 2 slots.
`if Array.length argv = 2 then "hello, " ^ argv.(1) else "usage: " ^ argv.(0) ^ " NAME"`.
explain: The reference is `if Array.length argv = 2 then "hello, " ^ argv.(1) else "usage: " ^ argv.(0) ^ " NAME"`. Slot 0 always holds the program's name, so one argument means a length of 2. Checking the length first means the function never reads a slot that is not there.
